clue.text: Colt supplier provides boss with fine gun

parts.note: a stud is a raised knob or boss on a surface
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: A dealer offers a commanding figure a fine firearm, the Colt revolver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' suggests the famous revolver, helped by 'gun', but here it is a young horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm keeping stallions for breeding produces foals, including young male horses.

clue.text: IOU storm maybe makes one apprehensive

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of the phrase are only one possible arrangement, so rework them

explanation.surface: A storm of unpaid IOUs leaves a debtor feeling nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' tells you IOU STORM is a possible version of the answer's letters: rearrange all eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone fearful and nervous, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Old fruit beginning to decay

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm

indicators.note: beginning to picks only the opening letter of the following word decay

explanation.surface: An ageing piece of fruit is starting to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old-fashioned is out of date, belonging to an earlier time.

clue.text: Newspaper column offering favourable situation?

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature promises readers an advantageous position.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase names a long-running newspaper property column about homes abroad, and literally means a sunny, enviable position.
explanation.definitionFit: A feature on buying sunny homes overseas carries this title; idiomatically the phrase means a privileged position in life.

clue.text: Blow for Pacino following film take

indicators.note: following places the actor's first name after the other pieces

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like a haze of mist
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
Al Pacino is the American actor

explanation.surface: A film take puts a hit on actor Al Pacino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a punch but is the verb or noun for wind: the answer is a cold wind of southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blows, and this is a strong northerly wind in the Rhône valley.

clue.text: Inflorescence inlaid in fancy merchandise

indicators.note: inlaid in says the letters sit set into the run of the words fancy merchandise

explanation.surface: A flower pattern is set into some ornate goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyme is a flower cluster where the central bloom opens first, a type of flower arrangement on a stem.

clue.text: Officer organised some US stadium

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: organised means the letters of some US are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A military officer arranged some American sports arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officer' is the abbreviation for colonel; 'organised' signals the anagram, giving OSSEUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The great amphitheatre of ancient Rome is the model of a large sports or games arena.

clue.text: Essentials count

explanation.surface: Counting what really matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The substance or core of something is its essential content; to count is to be important, as in 'it doesn't count'.

clue.text: Is that deliberate?

parts.note: read deliberate as a verb, to think hard, rather than the adjective intentional; the question asks for an idiom for straining to think

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an act was done on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to ponder hard, the effort of searching one's memory or reasoning intensely.

clue.text: Fission of atom in a liberal explosive

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters between the article and the liberal letter
fission splits an atom apart, so its letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Splitting the atom produces a liberal amount of explosive power.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as nuclear physics, but 'Fission of' is just an anagram signal, making MATO to sit 'in' A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatol is a high explosive made from TNT and ammonium nitrate, used in shells and bombs.

clue.text: Mark of injury allowed to become red

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a healed wound
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A wound mark is allowed to turn red.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant shade of red.

clue.text: Film figure supporting leader on right

parts.note: pro means in favour of or supporting
Duce, Italian for leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A movie person backs the leader of the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who finances and oversees the making of a movie is a key figure in cinema.

clue.text: X' almost paid fortune

indicators.note: almost removes the last letter of the word for X

parts.note: an X written at the end of a letter stands for a kiss
to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid

explanation.surface: A kiss almost settled one's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate or destiny, the fortune that awaits someone.

clue.text: Viewing depends on clear sun, maybe, without cloud

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
maybe signals the letters of clear sun can be put in another order

parts.note: a veil is something that clouds or obscures

explanation.surface: Sightseeing relies on a clear sun with no clouds about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: 'maybe' rearranges CLEAR SUN into SURLANCE, which wraps round VEIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveillance is close watching or observation of a person or place.

clue.text: Road, one settled in past, in workable condition

parts.note: via is Latin for road or way

indicators.note: in puts the one-and-settled pieces inside the word for past

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
I is the Roman numeral one
lit means alighted or settled, as a bird lit on a branch

explanation.surface: A road, once settled long ago, is still usable.
explanation.definitionFit: Viability is the state of being able to work or succeed, so a feasible condition.

clue.text: Silly article, almost sneering, unfortunately

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are mixed up
almost cuts the final letter from sneering

explanation.surface: A sneering article is unfortunately rather foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is the definition: geese are proverbially foolish. 'almost' drops the G and 'unfortunately' gives NSERINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anserine means goose-like, and a goose is a byword for a foolish person.

clue.text: Tenant's home almost demolished — is in for shock

indicators.note: is in says the two letters go inside the rebuilt letters
demolished means knocked down and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its possessive s supplies all its letters

indicators.note: almost cuts the final letter from home

explanation.surface: A renter's house is nearly knocked down, and they are stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenant's' keeps its S as a letter; 'almost' drops the E of home, 'demolished' gives ASTONHMENT, and 'is in' sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishment is great surprise, the feeling of being stunned.

clue.text: Making a pile in game, ending with secure grand

indicators.note: ending with puts the following pieces at the end

parts.note: nap is a card game, short for napoleon
to pin is to fasten or secure
G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Winning a fortune at cards, finishing with a guaranteed thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a pile' looks like getting rich, but it means raising the nap, the soft pile, on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The nap of cloth is its raised fibres, its pile, so raising those fibres is a finishing process.

clue.text: Crock possibly regarded as junk?

explanation.surface: An old pot might be thought of as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' reads as rubbish but is the Chinese sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A crock is an earthenware pot, a container; a junk is a Chinese sailing ship, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Red, this French rebel

parts.note: ce is French for this
to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: A French radical, a so-called Red, is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a cherry-coloured shade of red.

clue.text: Point about shortened projectile journalist repeated

indicators.note: about says the word for point goes round the next piece
shortened cuts the last letter off the projectile

parts.note: an arrow is a projectile shot from a bow
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter repeatedly makes a point about a short dart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' trims ARROW to ARRO, which PT goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, as the bird mimics speech.

clue.text: Indian, old pundit

parts.note: a sage is a wise person or pundit

explanation.surface: An Indian elder is a wise expert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Incitements limit us? Must be wrong

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of limit us are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a restriction on them must be mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that provoke a response, spurs to action.

clue.text: Character with a leaning to the right

definitions.text: Character with a leaning to the right

parts.words: Character with a leaning to the right
parts.note: reads like a person with right-wing views, but describes a printed letter that slopes rightward

explanation.surface: A person with conservative political sympathies.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanted type, used for emphasis, has letters that slope rightward.

clue.text: Toy production

explanation.surface: A toy production.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to fiddle with it; a stage production is a drama.

clue.text: Domestic device, good steamer repaired

indicators.note: repaired means fixed up, so the letters of steamer are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A good steamer, once mended, makes a handy household appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter is fitted in homes to record fuel used, a household instrument.
